items.title: Copilot in SharePoint adds generally available image, analytics, and metadata tools
items.summary: Microsoft says advanced Copilot in SharePoint capabilities are now generally available, including image generation and editing, AI-generated site analytics reports, and near-real-time metadata autofill. The features use Copilot Credits and are available to Copilot-licensed users, adding new AI-assisted workflows across SharePoint sites and document libraries.

items.title: Windows 11 26H1 preview adds WinRE remote-management support for MDM providers
items.summary: Microsoft’s October 28 preview update KB5127653 for Windows 11 version 26H1 adds a recovery remote-management plug-in that extends Windows Recovery Environment management capabilities for MDM providers. The update also includes other Windows improvements, but this new MDM recovery capability is the notable endpoint-management change.

items.title: Microsoft Copilot harness enters public preview in Foundry Agent Service
items.summary: Microsoft introduced the Copilot harness in Foundry Agent Service as a public preview, giving developers a managed way to build agents that reason, use tools, and complete complex, long-running tasks. The post also announced general availability of long-running resilience for hosted agents.

items.title: Visual Studio Marketplace adds secretless Trusted Publishing for extensions
items.summary: Microsoft announced Trusted Publishing for Visual Studio Marketplace extensions. GitHub Actions and Azure Pipelines can use verified federated identity to publish without storing a long-lived personal access token or publishing secret; existing PAT-based publishing remains available.

items.title: Microsoft makes Copilot UX components generally available with SPFx 1.24
items.summary: Microsoft made Copilot UX components generally available worldwide with SharePoint Framework 1.24, allowing developers to bring interactive dashboards, forms, and business actions into Copilot conversations. Components can also be reused in SharePoint, Teams, and Outlook; users need a Microsoft Copilot add-on license to render them in Copilot.

items.title: Copilot code review adds Max effort preview and generally available approvals
items.summary: GitHub added a Max effort level for Copilot code review in public preview and made Copilot approvals generally available. The combination is intended to provide a deeper review and an approval assessment within the pull-request review workflow.

items.title: Visual Studio Code 1.144 stable release expands agent workflows and continuity
items.summary: VS Code 1.144 shipped in the stable channel with expanded agent workflows, including agent sessions that continue across environments and client continuity supported by the Agent Host Protocol. The release also brings agent management and model-selection updates, making it a substantial IDE update for developers using Copilot agents.

items.title: GitHub brings Copilot Agent Merge into cloud pull requests
items.summary: GitHub integrated Agent Merge into pull requests on GitHub.com. Copilot can watch for blockers such as failing Actions workflows and merge conflicts and attempt to fix them; the cloud feature is available to paid Copilot users subject to organization and enterprise policies.

items.title: Microsoft and Syncfusion collaborate on open-source Blazor toolkit and contributions
items.summary: Microsoft announced a collaboration with Syncfusion to advance Blazor. Syncfusion has released a free, MIT-licensed component toolkit and contributed fixes and tests to ASP.NET Core and .NET scaffolding, adding reusable components while contributing directly to the platform.

items.title: IDC brings its Quanta research platform into Claude and adopts Claude company-wide
items.summary: Anthropic and IDC brought IDC Quanta into Claude, letting IDC customers query the research platform’s forecasts, market data, and analysis through Claude. IDC also rolled Claude out across its own business, combining a customer-facing research integration with a significant enterprise adoption.

items.title: Anthropic makes smart reports, surveys, and pooled budgets generally available for Claude Enterprise
items.summary: Anthropic made smart reports, in-app surveys, and pooled group budgets generally available for Claude Enterprise. The features give organizations new ways to understand Claude usage and outcomes, gather employee feedback, and set shared team spending limits.

items.title: SentinelOne plans to add Claude Mythos 5.1 to its Wayfinder security service
items.summary: SentinelOne announced plans to add Anthropic’s Claude Mythos 5.1 to Wayfinder Frontier AI Services, where it will be used alongside security experts to help identify and assess software risks. The announcement is a new security-services partnership development; SentinelOne described the addition as upcoming rather than already available.

items.title: Anthropic expands AI for Science support to foundations and research institutions
items.summary: Anthropic expanded its AI for Science program beyond individual researchers, partnering with 20 scientific foundations, institutions, and research groups and providing Claude credits for research. The announcement also highlights collaborations on safe lab-instrument use and AI-assisted analysis of scientific datasets, broadening the program’s institutional reach.

items.title: ChatGPT begins beta texting for dot agents via iMessage and RCS
items.summary: OpenAI began rolling out texting for its dot agent through iMessage and RCS, allowing users to send text, photos, and voice messages and receive proactive updates. The beta preview is for ChatGPT Pro users in the U.S., extending access to the agent beyond the ChatGPT app.

items.title: OpenAI offers eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers up to $500 monthly in API credits
items.summary: Eligible ChatGPT Pro and Business subscribers can claim monthly OpenAI API credits to build apps and agents, with the benefit reaching up to $500 per month. Pro allowances vary by tier, while Business credits are pooled by workspace and capped at $500 per monthly billing period.

items.title: Google announces Gemini 4 Carbon, its next frontier model
items.summary: Google announced Gemini 4 Carbon, describing it as its strongest model, with advances in cybersecurity and long-horizon capabilities. Access starts with a subset of cyber defenders and is planned to expand to trusted partners through the Fairwind Program before broader availability.

items.title: Gemini adds in-chat document creation, preview, and editing
items.summary: Gemini now lets users create, preview, and edit documents, PDFs, presentations, spreadsheets, code, and other files within a chat. Google says PDF preview and editing are available on web and mobile, while other listed formats are currently web-only; the capabilities are available to all Gemini app users in supported regions and languages.

items.title: Google reports Gemini classroom-study findings from the UK and Italy
items.summary: Google shared findings from studies in the UK and Italy on Gemini’s use in classrooms. The UK trial found AI tutoring provided math support comparable to human tutors for many students; the Italy study reported higher participation and more student-led collaboration when teachers used Gemini to co-design lessons.

items.title: FuriosaAI raises $620 million in Series D at $2.9 billion valuation
items.summary: South Korean AI-chip company FuriosaAI announced a $620 million Series D at a $2.9 billion post-money valuation. It said the funding will support production and deployment of its RNGD inference accelerator, software development, and work on a third-generation accelerator.

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for its 1-trillion-parameter Large 4 model
items.summary: Mistral released the weights for its improved Large 4 (Le Chonk), a one-trillion-parameter multimodal model, after additional training beyond its earlier public preview. The release emphasizes agentic coding, defensive cybersecurity, and self-hosting; the model is available under Mistral’s Ecosystem Open-Weight license, which includes a separate-license condition for some model-as-a-service uses.

items.title: Deepgram to acquire Daily, makers of open-source voice-agent framework Pipecat
items.summary: Deepgram announced it is acquiring Daily, the company behind the open-source Pipecat voice-agent framework, to combine it with Deepgram’s voice AI infrastructure. The companies say Pipecat will remain open source and vendor neutral; they did not disclose the deal amount.

items.title: Cohere announces initial Series E close targeting up to CAD $7 billion
items.summary: Cohere announced the initial close of a Series E round targeting up to CAD $7 billion, a figure the company says would imply a CAD $35.7 billion valuation. Schwarz Group is the lead investor; Cohere says the financing will support compute infrastructure, frontier models, and AI products for enterprises and governments, but the target is not the same as the amount already committed.

items.title: Digital Science acquires Jenni AI, bringing its AI research-writing platform into its scholarly-data ecosystem
items.summary: Digital Science acquired Jenni AI, an AI-native research and writing platform used by more than 8 million students and researchers in 189 countries. The planned integration with Digital Science’s research data, starting with its Dimensions database, aims to connect AI-assisted discovery and writing with published research sources and citation checking.
